questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To experience North American college-culture and then the nature in British Columbia!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say it was fairly easy. The GoGlobal office is very good at helping incoming students. Just make sure to also look into things yourself and go to the introdays and so on.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A general introday for exchangestudents.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Seriously do not hesitate to reach out to Go Global they are very helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different types of dorms. Make sure to choose one where you get your own room. Highly recomment Fairview Crescent or Walter Gage!!

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Fairview and Walter Gage have units of 4-6 people where you share a kitchen. Just be aware that it comes without pots, plates and what not. Would highly recomment going to the SPCA thriftstore to get what you need though!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That the housing is kinda crusty but the people are amazing. And it is a special experience to live on campus. Do not miss out on going to Pacific Spirit Park and the beaches around campus. They are amazing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was approximately as annoying as I thought it would be. I am also a graduate student though, which makes registration much more annoying.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: For grad-students. Send email to professer teaching the course you wish where you introduce yourself and clarify why you are eligible to take the course. Wait for their reply. Then forward the email to the department offering the course, and then the faculty for grad-studies. And then Go Global. There is also a whole bunch of course registration for EVERYONE beforehand by GoGlobal, which does not really matter when you need grad courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: GoGlobal and then reaching out to the professors and departments. Also I showed up at the math departments office in the first week because they had not replied to my emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 2/3 of the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are a grad student - do email the relevant professorts before the term starts so that you can get enrolled fast. Everyone are very busy in the first weeks of class, so you get the best help beforehand.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My classes where either way too easy or way too hard. But I kinda knew that getting into it.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: So I had one exceptionally easy introductory statistics course (545A+B), which I picked cause I knew it would be easy. And then 2 very hard math courses - the prerequisites they listed were not quite explicit enough, so my background was a bit insufficient. Both of them were only assignment/take home exams and they were still hard work. It is possible to do it, just don't expect the level 500 math courses to be a lower workload than graduate math courses at KU :)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Fairly similar honestly. A bit more discussion-based, but not by much.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: STAT545A+B Exploratory Data Analysis, MATH503 Discrete Mathematics and MATH516 Partial Differential Equations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both math courses were good and very interesting. And the professors were excellent. I was just struggling because my background is in probability and not so much functional analysis and algebra :)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping is very expensive (go to NO FRILLS or T&T. And the housing comes without ANYTHING.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food. 50DKK for organic yoghurt... And then you can go eat out for 75DKK, which makes no sense

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are SO many clubs! Join the VOC for hardcore hiking and rockclimbing. Surf club for Tofino-trip. And the Ski and Board club for renting gear for free.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many things. Calender parties, weird social events with student housing and also sometimes faculty-specific things I think. You can also do sports - swimming, yoga, pilates jiujitsu and what not. Just sign up!!!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: VOC (Varsity Outdoor Club) a very nice community and great for giving you inspiration for what trips could be nice. And the UBC-filmsociety. You pay 5 dollars ONCE and then they screen 4 movies every week in a small actual cinema. And they have some nice niche stuff. And use the libraries there. They have both course-books but also A LOT of fiction.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Squamish and Whistler for hiking and skiing! And to Vancouver Island! Also a trip to Seattle is worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. But I was also mainly close to other exchange students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the people in your classes! Most Canadians are fairly open. And join some of the VOC-trips.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None in particular. It is more normal to small-talk with strangers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Small-talking with strangers is very cute when you are an exchange-student feeling lonely. Also Canadians are nice. But Vancouverites are less so than other Canadians.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Just stay on top of the administrative things cause they are not that bad, and try to not have courses that you absolutely NEED to take. Be flexible, then it will be very easy.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being in such a beatiful place and experiencing the whole college-culture. It is crazy.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
